name: Dev Ferris
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: Dev ran the pawn counter through years when half his customers didn't want to be recognized. Releasing a paid ticket is often easy. Getting someone to believe the account is settled can take another decade. People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Dev by a small Friday habit. Dev knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: Somebody paid the ticket years ago and never removed it. I can tell from the tear. I want the old owner to find that out from me because we parted on ugly terms.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. Dev has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Dev grins on one side while the eyes stay serious during a conversation.
personality: Dev always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Dev is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To show the former owner when the ticket was actually paid.
family: Edmund Porter is Dev’s second cousin. Dev offers the first invitation. Edmund gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The crane shadow*, Edmund says, “I can no longer climb the cab ladder. I stood inside its shadow and taught a child the controls from memory.”
connections: Iris Cade. The teacher and the pawnbroker make the call that establishes whether the old ticket was settled.
